Codex's automated review bot found a real gap in the CLAUDE-034 fix commit (independently confirmed by Claude before ChatGPT's formal CHANGES_REQUIRED handoff arrived): migration 0007's BEFORE INSERT trigger only governs future inserts, so any queue_entries row created before this migration runs would keep its pre-existing ID-derived public_display_label forever, meaning the new unauthenticated waiting-room snapshot could still publish ID-derived labels for upgraded/pre-existing data. Fixed by adding a one-time backfill block to migration 0007 that regenerates every existing row's label using the identical collision-safe random generation the trigger uses, scoped per session -- confirmed harmless no-op on a fresh/empty database. Added a real-Postgres regression test that disables the trigger, inserts a row with the exact pre-migration insecure label (simulating real historical data), re-enables the trigger, then re-runs the backfill logic directly and asserts the label is no longer ID-derived. Verified: full suite 53/53 (3 consecutive runs of the affected test file), typecheck/lint/format clean. CI green on this exact head (run 34066463561).
